official_measurement_examples.name: Plan-led viability
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current guidance says viability assessment is primarily a plan-making exercise and policy-compliant applications under up-to-date policies should generally be assumed viable.

official_measurement_examples.name: Benchmark land value method
official_measurement_examples.fact: Benchmark land value should be based on existing use value plus a reasonable landowner premium, with policy and abnormal costs reflected; it is not simply the price paid for land.

official_measurement_examples.name: Price-paid limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government viability guidance states the price paid for land is not a relevant justification for failing to comply with plan policy, while HMLR Price Paid Data is transaction evidence with registration timing and coverage limitations.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 policy-appraisal values
official_measurement_examples.fact: MHCLG published Land value estimates for policy appraisal 2023 on 16 March 2026 and explicitly states they are generic policy-appraisal values, not market values for individual sites.

official_measurement_examples.name: Vacant Building Credit
official_measurement_examples.fact: Vacant Building Credit offsets relevant existing vacant floorspace against affordable-housing contribution calculations where the policy applies; it is not a blanket affordable-housing exemption or planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Green Belt Golden Rules
official_measurement_examples.fact: Where the NPPF Golden Rules apply, current viability guidance says site-specific viability should not be used to reduce the specified developer contributions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Costs and infrastructure
official_measurement_examples.fact: Viability costs can include abnormal costs, SuDS, utilities, CIL, section 106 and BNG; including a cost does not prove the underlying constraint, quote or capacity has been verified for a parcel.

official_measurement_examples.name: Viability outcome limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A viability appraisal is financial planning evidence and does not determine title ownership, planning permission, exact buildable area or final development yield.

core_rules: viability assessment is not planning permission
benchmark land value is not simply purchase price
EUV plus method must retain policy and site-cost context
generic policy-appraisal land values are not site market values
Price Paid Data is not a parcel BLV determination
recent Price Paid Data can be incomplete
Vacant Building Credit is not automatic affordable-housing exemption
Green Belt Golden Rules viability limitation must be retained
cost assumptions do not prove infrastructure capacity
viability evidence does not determine land ownership
policy-compliant assumption must retain up-to-date policy context
no parcel viability clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG, Homes England, HM Land Registry and GOV.UK sources checked on 2026-07-26. The 16 March 2026 land-value estimates and 26 June 2026 Price Paid Data release were retained with EUV+, VBC, Golden Rules and market-data limitations; no parcel promotion.
